title: Electrostatic work A→B
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the work done by the electrostatic force from A to B using the work-energy theorem, arriving at W = 0.5mgh.

title: Electrostatic work B→C
description: Important: Recognizes that B and C lie on the same equipotential surface, so the electrostatic force does zero work between them.

title: Total work A→C
description: Essential: Correctly sums the work from A→B and B→C to find the total work done by the electrostatic force from A to C as 0.5mgh.

title: Potential difference formula
description: Important: Applies the definition of potential difference U_AC = W_AC / (-q) correctly, accounting for the test charge's sign.

title: Final numerical answers
description: Essential: Provides both final answers in the correct form: (1) 0.5mgh or mgh/2, and (2) -mgh/(2q).

title: Sign error in potential
description: Pitfall: Forgets the negative sign in the potential difference formula (U = W/(-q)) or misplaces the sign of the charge q, leading to an incorrect sign for U_AC.

title: Equipotential reasoning
description: Optional: Explains that B and C are equidistant from charge Q, thus on the same equipotential, justifying zero work from B to C.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Expresses final answers with correct implied units (Joules for work, Volts for potential difference).
